question_text: Name a plant that has a single fruit developing from the entire inflorescence. What is such a fruit called?

page_header: Section A — Very Short Answer Question

steps.label: The plant
lines: inflorescence, with its axis and bracts,
steps.why: The scale is the point - not one flower but the WHOLE inflorescence becomes one fruit body.
common_mistakes: Naming custard apple. That is an aggregate fruit from ONE flower, not from an inflorescence.
steps.memory_tip: Pineapple and jackfruit - many flowers fused into one big fruit.
steps.margin_note: Either plant earns the mark; the inflorescence line shows why.

steps.label: Name of such a fruit

lines.text: Such a fruit is called a composite fruit

steps.why: Composite is the asked name; sorosis is the technical term for the pineapple/jackfruit type of composite fruit.
common_mistakes: Writing aggregate. Aggregate = one flower; composite = whole inflorescence.
steps.memory_tip: Composite - composed of the whole inflorescence.
steps.margin_note: Composite is the mark; sorosis in brackets is the finishing touch.
